record.title: Data4 and EDF announce a long-term nuclear electricity allocation for French data centers
record.summary: EDF and Data4 announced a 12-year Nuclear Production Allocation Contract (CAPN) for Data4’s French data centers. EDF’s French release says the agreement allocates Data4 a 40 MW share of EDF’s operating nuclear fleet, with costs and production-volume risks shared, and forecasts first deliveries from 2026 at about 230 GWh per year. Data4 describes it as the first CAPN signed by a French data-center operator. The sources establish the announced contract terms, not actual Data4 deliveries, metered volumes, the contract tariff, or allocation to AI workloads.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: EDF and Data4 publicly announced a 12-year Nuclear Production Allocation Contract for Data4’s French data centers in September 2025.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: EDF says the agreement allocates Data4 a 40 MW share of EDF’s operating nuclear fleet, with costs and production-volume risks shared according to actual production.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: EDF and Data4 forecast initial delivery from 2026 at around 230 GWh per year.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected sources do not establish actual Data4 delivery or metered volume, contract tariff, carbon-intensity accounting, or electricity use by AI workloads.

evidence_gaps.description: The 2026 delivery start is a forecast; no actual allocated or metered Data4 volume was verified.
The press releases do not disclose the contract tariff or allocation of electricity to AI workloads.

brief.importance_rationale: If delivered as announced, the 12-year nuclear-production allocation could shape a French data-center operator’s low-carbon power procurement and provide a concrete contract mechanism as compute demand grows. The consequence is notable but specific to one operator and a forecast; actual deliveries, tariffs, metered volumes and AI workload use remain unverified.
limitations: The evidence is two company press releases, not an independently inspected contract or metering record.
Around 230 GWh per year is a forecast, not a demonstrated delivery volume.
No tariff, hourly delivery profile, grid effect, carbon-accounting method, or AI workload-specific electricity allocation is provided.
The announcement concerns one operator and cannot establish broad data-center demand or nuclear supply sufficiency.
brief.summary: EDF and Data4 announced a 12-year Nuclear Production Allocation Contract (CAPN) for Data4’s French data centers. EDF’s French release says the agreement allocates Data4 a 40 MW share of EDF’s operating nuclear fleet, with costs and production-volume risks shared, and forecasts first deliveries from 2026 at about 230 GWh per year. Data4 describes it as the first CAPN signed by a French data-center operator. The sources establish the announced contract terms, not actual Data4 deliveries, metered volumes, the contract tariff, or allocation to AI workloads.

technical.claimed_result: The companies say the arrangement will provide Data4 with low-carbon electricity and long-term predictability; these benefits are company claims and were not independently measured.
technical.demonstrated_result: EDF and Data4 published the contract announcement and described its terms; actual electricity delivery is not demonstrated.
technical.implementation_status: Contract announced; first deliveries were forecast to start in 2026. No actual Data4 delivery or meter evidence was found in this check.
technical.mechanism: A Nuclear Production Allocation Contract gives Data4 a stated share of output capacity from EDF’s operating nuclear fleet for a long term, with production costs and volume risks shared.
technical.regime: One 12-year agreement for Data4’s French data-center infrastructure; announced in September 2025; initial delivery forecast from 2026; 40 MW share and around 230 GWh annual forecast as stated by the companies.
technical.reproducibility: Not a scientific experiment. The announcement was directly inspected on EDF’s French-language site and Data4’s official site; contract execution and energy delivery were not independently audited.
technical.strongest_baseline: Data4’s previously contracted solar and wind PPAs, which EDF and Data4 say the nuclear allocation supplements; comparative price, hourly profile and emissions outcomes were not supplied.

brief.title: Data4 and EDF announce a long-term nuclear electricity allocation for French data centers
brief.why_it_matters: The agreement is a concrete example of a long-duration nuclear-power allocation mechanism aimed at data-center supply. If delivered as described, it could affect how operators plan low-carbon electricity procurement while compute demand grows. The specific customer, forecast terms and absence of verified delivery limit what can be inferred about broader supply or AI energy use.
